questions.q: Why does Overlook's database need differential backups at all, given that automated full backups already run weekly?
options: A database with real daily activity can't rely on a once-a-week snapshot alone — differentials keep the gap between the last full and now small
Differential backups replace full backups entirely on Azure SQL Database
Full backups are not reliable enough to trust on their own
Azure requires at least two backup types to be configured before a database can go online
questions.explain: The differential exists specifically to close the gap a weekly full backup alone would leave, without the cost of running full backups constantly.

questions.q: If Azure's full backup ran Sunday, what does Wednesday's automated differential backup actually capture?
options: Everything changed since Sunday's full backup (not since Monday's or Tuesday's differential)
Only the changes that happened on Wednesday itself
Everything changed since the very first backup ever taken
Nothing — only full backups capture real data, differentials are metadata only
questions.explain: A differential is always relative to the last full backup, so it keeps growing day over day until the next full resets it — exactly the Lesson 2 planning logic, now running automatically.

questions.q: Why does a differential backup stay 'fast enough to run every 12-24 hours without a noticeable backup window'?
options: It only copies pages that changed since the last full backup, which is a small fraction of the total data most days
It skips the Billing table entirely to save time
It runs at a lower compression ratio than a full backup
Azure throttles differential backups to run only on weekends
questions.explain: Copying only changed pages (rather than the whole database) is what keeps a differential cheap, even though the amount it captures grows day by day until the next full.

questions.q: Why can't you query a day-by-day differential backup job history on Azure SQL Database the way you could with on-prem msdb?
options: Azure SQL Database doesn't expose that level of backup-job detail to the DBA, consistent with the PaaS trade-off from Lesson 4
Differential backups aren't actually logged anywhere on any platform
msdb doesn't exist on any version of SQL Server
Azure only retains backup job history for Managed Instance, never for Azure SQL Database
questions.explain: On this PaaS tier, you confirm the overall backup chain's health (e.g. via earliestRestoreDate) rather than inspecting a per-job history log the way on-prem msdb would allow.

questions.q: During an automatic point-in-time restore on Azure SQL Database, who decides which differential backup to apply?
options: Azure selects it automatically as part of assembling the full + differential + log restore chain
The DBA must manually specify the exact differential backup file to restore
No differential is ever used during a point-in-time restore — only full and log backups apply
The database administrator must first delete all other differentials before restoring
questions.explain: Azure SQL Database's point-in-time restore assembles the correct full, differential, and log chain automatically — the DBA never manually picks which differential to use.
